blocks.text: My Lord, we'd reached the first of the interviews concerning [Baby Q], which is very much towards the end of bundle 2.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: DS DANIELLE STONIER (continued)
Examination-in-chief by MR ASTBURY (continued )
The first of these interviews regarding [Baby Q] took place on 5 July 2018.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes, that's correct.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: It began with the usual introductions and the officer began: Okay, so during this interview we're going to talk about [Baby Q]. Okay? At 04.09 hours on 22/6/2016 [Baby Q] was born to [Mother of Baby Q] and [Father of Baby Q]. At 09.10 hours on 25/6/16, [Baby Q] collapsed. Okay? What can you tell us about the care that you offered to [Baby Q], Lucy?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: So I believe on that morning I was looking after [Baby Q] and another baby that was in nursery 1. [Baby Q] was in nursery 2 and from what I remember I was alerted by another member of staff that he'd vomited and needed some support when I was in the other nursery. That's all I can remember from memory.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Lucy Letby confirmed that she had the relevant notes and that she had been [Baby Q]'s designated nurse on the relevant shift. She was asked: Okay. And, just generally, what can you tell us about the clinical position of [Baby Q] when you took over his care on that morning?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Um, [Baby Q] had a low temperature, which had needed his incubator to be increased and also that he was tachycardic.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: At the time you took over?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. So what was being done about that?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: So his be -- his incubator was being increased to combat the temperature.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. So in terms of what you needed to do with him from the beginning of the shift, moving forward with his care plan, what -- what was in your mind that you were going to progress with that?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: With his care for the day?
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I would be reviewing what medications he was due and when, how often he was needing observations, if and when he was being fed and when they were due, when his nappy change would be due.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. Was he ventilated?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Lucy Letby was unable to recall which other baby was in nursery 2 at the time, but she did remember that Mary Griffith was the other nurse working in there. She was asked: Okay. So with regards to his position when you took over that morning, were there any concerns for him at that time?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: That he had a low temperature.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. Sorry, just on that point, were you concerned such that you were happy to leave [Baby Q]?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Leave in what way?
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Well, you said that -- at the initial start of the interview you gave you said you were alerted to the fact that he'd vomited [as read].
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: So where were you?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I believe I was in nursery 1 with the other baby.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Right, okay. So the point I'm saying is [Baby Q] was well enough to be left?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Yes. Okay. The next entry is at 9.10. Explain that entry to us.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Okay. So I have written that he was attended to by Staff Nurse Lappalainen, who I think was in charge that day.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I think I'd been in nursery 1 and I came back out to come to nursery 2 and saw that [Baby Q] was having intervention and that I've written, from here, he had vomited, mottled, desaturation in (sic) and had needed Neopuff and suction and that [Dr A] had attended.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay so at 09.10 when you handed him over, why was that?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I haven't handed him over. This -- Staff Nurse Lappalainen had attended to [Baby Q], so she had gone to him for a reason.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Because you were out in the other nursery?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Do you know what alerted her to go in and attend to him?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. And you were elsewhere dealing with another baby?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I believe so, yes.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Between 08.00 and 09.00 hours Lucy Letby explained that she'd completed [Baby Q]'s observations, he'd had a slightly high respiratory rate, and she increased the temperature of his incubator. And she was asked: Would that -- is that something that needs any kind of treatment, the increased respiratory rate?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No, so usually, you just find -- usually if they enter this other band in here on the chart --
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Right, okay.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: -- then we would -- you would let somebody know or the doctors would review them when they were next on the unit.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: So the doctors usually attend to do the ward round at 9 o'clock. I don't think I escalated that at that point.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. Can you remember any other treatment around the observations just prior to your leaving?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Lucy Letby confirmed from the notes that she'd not fed [Baby Q] and he was receiving Babiven and lipids.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Question: Did you communicate with any other members of staff that you were leaving the nursery?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I think Mary Griffith was in the room when I left and I think I told her.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. Do you remember when you told -- you think you told Mary what -- what might Mary have been doing at the time?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I think she was with another baby in the nursery.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Was she doing anything to that baby, treating that baby at all?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I think she was at the incubator, yes, from what I remember.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. When -- do you remember the words you said to her?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. So how did you first become aware that [Baby Q] needed to be attended to?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I think from memory I came out of whatever I was doing in nursery 1 and saw that people with [Baby Q] in nursery 2.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: What were they doing?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I think when I went in they were giving him support with the Neopuff.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. And who was that?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I think it was Minna Lappalainen.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Just on her own?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No, I think -- I don't know if a doctor was there or Mary was there as well.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. So what did you do then? What observations did you make?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I don't remember entirely but I believe he was moved into nursery 1 and we started CPAP on him.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. Did you see the vomit?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I don't remember the vomit.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. So where put he'd:
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: "... vomited clear fluid nasally and from mouth, desaturation, bradycardia, mottled ++."
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Were they your observations or were they what you were told?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I believe they were what I was told.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. And the Neopuff and suction applied, are they actions that you've done or actions that people who were treating him have done?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No, I think they were actions by other people.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. So did you -- I don't know if I asked you, sorry, did you see the vomit?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No, I don't think I saw the vomit.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: But that's how it was described to you?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: And so after you were told the description of what some of your colleagues have seen what did you think about what had happened to [Baby Q]?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I was unsure as to why he would have been vomiting.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. What are the implications of a clear fluid, nasally and from the mouth?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: That he's vomited, but he hasn't got anything in his stomach to vomit, so it's clearly bodily fluids that he's vomiting.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: So when you left -- did you do a procedure for [Baby Q] then prior to leaving?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I've documented observations at 9 o'clock.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. Did you administer anything to [Baby Q] before you left?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I don't know from memory I'd have to check.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: If you could that would be great.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No, I don't think so.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: The observations at 9 o'clock, how long does that process take?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Not long because we read them from the monitor, then we count the respiratory rate.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Are we talking seconds, minutes?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: A minute maybe.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: I presume if you were concerned you -- would you stay with [Baby Q]?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Did you see the mottling on [Baby Q]?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I don't remember.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Right, okay. And was this vomit and desaturation -- was that expected from your point of view, from what you'd observed from [Baby Q]?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No, but sometimes babies do vomit and they can -- that can lead them to have a desaturation because they have vomited.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. So the next line is:
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: "[Dr A] attended. Air ++ aspirated from NG tube. Transferred to nursery 1."
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Okay. So the air ++, are they your entries and your observations?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I'm not sure whether I aspirated the tube or whether that was done by somebody else whilst I was there.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Right okay. So air ++ from the NG tube, how does that happen?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: How do you get air in the --
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I am not sure. Sometimes if babies are vomiting they can gulp down air.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Right. Are there any other ways that air can get there, air ++ especially?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I'm not sure.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: If the baby's maybe got some sort of blockage in the bowel, that air isn't passing through the rectum.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Any others?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No, not that I know of.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Who contacted the registrar?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I'm not sure.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. Was he one of the people that were in attendance when you first became aware of members of staff treating [Baby Q]?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I don't recall specifically who -- if he was there or not at that moment, no.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. And you don't recall whether you aspirated the tube?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. Did you continue to care for him after that?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Um, I think so, yes.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: As designated nurse, I mean.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Lucy Letby explained that [Baby Q]'s parents visited later that day. They were upset that nobody had told them about what had happened. She and [Nurse B] had apologised that it must have been an oversight. Whilst [Baby Q] was being treated as the priority, they had not had chance to contact the parents. And she was asked: Okay, are there any other observations you've got regarding [Baby Q]?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Can you give us any explanation as to why this event happened, where he vomited and collapsed?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: And the interview, insofar as [Baby Q] was concerned, was suspended at that point.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Thank you.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Moving on to the second occasion when Lucy Letby was asked questions about [Baby Q], we can see that took place on 12 June 2019.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes, that's right.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: It began with the observation: Lucy, I'm going to ask you about [Baby Q].
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: The officers then summarised the previous interview concerning [Baby Q]. Ms Letby was told and then asked: Mary Griffith states Nurse Letby was also caring for a second baby in nursery 1. Which baby were you caring for in nursery 1?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I think her name was B.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: That's our editing, the full name was given.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes, it was, yes.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Well, certainly the first name: You left the nursery shortly before [Baby Q] collapsed?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Right.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Do you agree with that?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Lucy, explain to me what did to [Baby Q] before leaving nursery 2 to cause his collapse?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I didn't cause his collapse, I checked his observations.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. And what did his observations suggest? Was he stable?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: That his temperature had decreased, so I've increased his incubator.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Mm-hm. Was he stable at that time Lucy?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: He's got a rise in respiratory rate and heart rate but it's not going completely into the warning area so...
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. Would you class [Baby Q] as stable at that time?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Would you have left the nursery if he wasn't?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: What did you do?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: And I've asked Mary to keep an eye on him in my absence.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: What did you do to him, Lucy, to cause him to collapse?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I took his observations, I didn't cause a collapse.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: There was two people in the room, Lucy, wasn't there, Mary Griffith and you?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Mary was treating another baby and then [Baby Q] collapses. Are you responsible for his collapse?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Lucy Letby was informed of Dr Evans' opinion regarding air via the NGT into his, that meaning [Baby Q]'s, stomach.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I don't think I fed him at that point, did I? I think I just did observations.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: [Baby Q] suffered a single collapse; do you agree?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Did you inject air into [Baby Q]?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Were you responsible for his collapse?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Lucy, are you responsible for the attempted murder of [Baby Q]?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay. It's quarter to 12 and the interview is now at an end.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: That was the conclusion of that particular interview.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: The third and final occasion when Lucy Letby was asked questions about [Baby Q] was on 11 November 2020.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: The interview begins: You were away from [Baby Q] when he suffered a desaturation and vomited. You denied causing [Baby Q] to collapse and denied causing him any harm. Is that accurate?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Is there anything you want to add regarding that?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: At 09.00 hours you completed [Baby Q]'s observations and he was due a feed. However, this was not given. When Minna attends to [Baby Q] after his desaturation she evidences that he had quite a bit of mucus and he'd been sick. If it wasn't feed, what had you given to him to cause him to vomit?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I didn't give him anything. If it's not documented that I didn't feed him then I didn't give him anything.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Was it air that you administered?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Did you deliberately leave the room to blame the collapse on Mary Griffith and Minna?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No, the baby in nursery 1 was due cares at that time.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Dr Lakin from Alder Hey Children's Hospital shows that he made a quick recovery. Do you agree with that?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yeah, that's actually what happened, yeah. That's not stay that he wouldn't have recovered if he had stayed with us on the unit.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: The officers summarised the statement of [Dr D], who describes [Baby Q] as having been stable overnight on the shift on the 24th into 25 June: Is that just a coincidence then, is it?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yeah. Babies can deteriorate any time.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: At 13.30 hours on the 25th you messaged [Nurse E] and said in speech marks, "Aspirated". Was he aspirated?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I don't recall, but I think "aspirated" meant that when a baby's vomited and then inhaled the fluid back into their lungs, that's an aspiration.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Do you remember doing that?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Doing what?
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Aspirating.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No, so aspirated would be me withdrawing the feed from him and aspiration -- if I'm saying that he's aspirated, it means he's been sick and then inhaled some of the fluid, which is like pneumonia.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Okay.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I am saying he's aspirated then, that's the context I think.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: At 22.46 hours on the 25th you messaged [Dr A] and asked if you should be worried about what Dr Gibbs was asking; do you recall that?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: What was that about then, Lucy?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I became aware that Dr Gibbs had been asking why -either why or where I was when [Baby Q] collapsed, why I wasn't in the nursery with him, and it was discussed that obviously I had two babies in separate nurseries and I was concerned that I was going to be -- you know, be a problem that I wasn't there at the time.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Were you trying to seek his reassurance?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yeah, I suppose so, yeah. I wouldn't have just left a baby unattended: Mary was in the room and Minna was just outside at the desk.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: That wasn't trying to blame the others?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No, there was no blame to be apportioned. It was just that I had not left the nursery unattended to tend to my other baby.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: At 16.44 on the 26th you messaged [Nurse E] and told her [Baby Q] had NEC and that [Dr A] had told you; is that correct?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I don't recall that specifically, no.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Did [Baby Q] have NEC?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I'm not sure without looking.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: [Nurse E] tells you that [Baby Q] may have volvulus; do you remember that?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: STONIER

blocks.text: Right.

blocks.text: Well, exactly. Many days. So I don't think that saying that we're going to have a four-day gap or a five-day gap in fact is prejudicial to anyone because the evidence is going to span a long period in any event.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: Therefore given that we are losing so many days, of necessity, I don't want to lose any more unless it is by reason of necessity. So my inclination at the moment -- I'm not saying this as a final decision but I thought it might help if I expressed my view at this stage and I will hear what Mr Johnson says -- my inclination is that as soon as we are in a position to proceed with the defence case and whatever evidence is called on behalf of the defence, then we start that, even if there's going to be a four-day gap after that.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Well, I should say, with respectful agreement, that whereas ordinarily that would be something we would strive to avoid, given the inevitability of breaks in the course of Ms Letby's evidence, if that is where we go, whatever we do there are going to be breaks here and there. Therefore, we understand why your Lordship takes the view you do.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: To assist as best as we can at this point, it would seem to us that it is unlikely we would start again with the jury until Tuesday.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: That's what I'm thinking at the moment.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: What I'm thinking, and I will hear from Mr Johnson, but if it's anticipated that essentially tomorrow is going to be taken up with legal argument and discussion about arrangements so far as the defendant giving evidence is concerned, and I can say this to assist you, that I am understanding of the difficulties --
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Thank you.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: -- and there will be accommodation.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: We're grateful for that, my Lord.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: I'm conscious of (a) the situation of the defendant giving evidence in stressful circumstances and there will be breaks and the total period per day will not be what I consider to be excessive.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: We're grateful. We'll deal with that and assist the court when we come to it, but so far as we can assist right now that seems to be the way the timings are with evidence to commence on Tuesday, or possibly Friday if Tuesday is required for any further legal deliberations.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: Yes. In other words, I don't think the discussion about the arrangements will take very long at all.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: We don't think it will either, my Lord.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: I would have thought minutes, frankly.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Certainly not as long as the size of the bundle might perhaps have otherwise led the court to believe.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: There we are. As I said, I understand what the situation is. I'll hear what Mr Johnson says.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Is there anything else you want to say, Mr Myers?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Not at this stage, no.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: Mr Johnson?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Nothing constructive to contribute, thank you, my Lord.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: I think as far as the jury is concerned, we can say they won't be required tomorrow but they should be prepared to attend, and should attend, on Tuesday --
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: -- unless tomorrow afternoon they are informed to the contrary.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: The usual arrangement with which they're familiar.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes. Mr Myers and I have discussed the essential basis, or at least I believe we've discussed the essential basis, of the submission and if we receive something in writing, we'll try and have something in writing with your Lordship by tomorrow morning.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Necessarily, given the limited number of hours between now and then, it won't be very long, but it may be all the better for that, because it's a fairly fundamental point.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Well, let's wait and see. I entirely agree that that's the appropriate way of dealing with it. So that's what I'll do, then: call the jury back and say that they won't be required tomorrow but will, subject to some notification to the contrary, be required on Tuesday.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Good. Thank you very much indeed.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: (In the presence of the jury)

You will recall many months ago when we first met and this case started that I said I would deal with all questions of law that arose. I've got to deal with an issue of law, I can't deal with it this afternoon, it's going to require tomorrow for it to be dealt with. So what I'm saying is that tomorrow you will not be required to attend at court. It will be the start for you of what will be a four-day weekend because it's then Saturday, Sunday and Monday is the first of the three May public holidays.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: But you will be required on Tuesday to come back and continue with the trial, unless for some unexpected reason, so I'm saying that in the spirit of optimism, you are notified to the contrary tomorrow afternoon in the usual way that you are if you're told you're not required to come on the next sitting day.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: You've got your list here. You know that we're coming up to a period where we are sitting intermittently, essentially, rather consecutively.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: So looking at the document, Tuesday will, unless you are notified to the contrary, be a sitting day.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Then we have Wednesday and Thursday off. Friday will then be the next sitting day. Then we have another public holiday. Then we've got Monday, Tuesday and that Wednesday off, the 9th and 10th, then we're back on Thursday and so on and so forth. All right?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: That's the best I can do. All right? Thank you very much for your patience, your understanding and continued diligent attention to this case and to your responsibilities as jurors in the case, which I remind you, for the umpteenth time: no communication by any means with anyone about anything to do with
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: this case and no research about anyone or anything to do with this case.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Tuesday of next week, please. Thank you very much.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: (In the absence of the jury)

Just for the record, my Lord, and to reflect what I understand is the agreed position, it's actually incorporated in the admissions that all the interviews are in in case anything has been edited out that's relevant or becomes relevant, I should say, and the same applies, by an understanding, as I understand it to be, about the Facebook material as well. There's an awful lot of material. There's a schedule to come, but I understand the position that as between us we are agreed that should anything arise in the course of the defendant's evidence that converts something from apparent irrelevance to relevance, then there's no issue about it being referred to.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: That's agreed, of course, my Lord. It goes both ways.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: Exactly. Clearly it's evidence in the case and, if required and if necessary, reference can be made to it, even though it's not directly been referred to at this stage.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: No, we understand.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: Whilst we've been going through those agreed facts in relation to interviews it occurred to me because when I was cross-referencing the summaries of the interviews that were given to the jury, helpfully, at the end of each baby, I realised there were slight, very slight, differences, but that's not in the least bit critical. I think it's very helpful to do it in the way it was done. If I may say so. The jury will appreciate that they've got just a small proportion of the total interviews, which would otherwise run to many volumes.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Enormous, yes.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: Good.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: We're grateful for the work that's actually gone into them, no criticism, but they were huge to begin with.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: I know. You knew that I was encouraging as much editing as possible and it was on that understanding that they were all in evidence and it was just basically trying to put before the jury what was salient.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: I know certainly Mr Astbury, Mr Maher and Ms Clancy have been heavily involved in reducing them and we are both grateful to them for doing that work.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: I'm very grateful for all the work that's been done.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: I'm not going to spend time now going through the proposed arrangements so far as the defendant giving evidence are concerned, I'd rather that we all got your document and started reading that at this stage. But as I've indicated, unless Mr Johnson wants to make any specific representations I'm essentially, so far as timetabling, of the mind that we should have around one-hour slots, then a more substantial than tenminute break, so that we have essentially in the region of no more than 4 hours a day.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: We'd be grateful for that. We can look at the actual timing when we look at the arrangements, but we were going to ask for something along those lines, my Lord. We'll come to that.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: Exactly. All right, good --
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: I should say the submission has now been sent.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: We are putting together a bundle of documents to assist because certain transcripts are referred to, so we shall put those together and make sure your Lordship and my learned friends have those as quickly as possible, but we certainly didn't want to delay the receipt of the submission itself because it will be plain enough what we're referring to from the submission.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: That's helpful. Thank you very much.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Mr Johnson, as and when, don't worry too much about rushing your response. I'd rather that you were content that you had covered the ground you wanted to cover, not necessarily in as much detail as you may want, but at least address the points you want to make, whatever they may be.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Mr Myers?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes, we would be grateful if we could see Ms Letby now.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: Thank you. The court will sit at 10.30 tomorrow then.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: (The court adjourned until 10.30 am on Friday, 28 April 2023)
